layout_summary: A tall two-column poster on pure white: a red patent stiletto bleeds off the upper-left corner and its heel melts downward into a jar of spread in the lower-left, while a stacked film-title typographic lockup occupies the right half at mid-height. A single full-width red one-liner sits as a footer band at the very bottom, centred on the canvas.

scene.subject: A glossy scarlet patent-leather pointed-toe stiletto pump, seen in profile, tilted toe-up toward the upper right so its sole and opening face the viewer's left. The shoe's slim stiletto heel does not end in a tip — it stretches downward into a long tapering stem that changes material partway, turning from red lacquer into thick golden-brown caramel spread, and splits into three downward-pointing prongs like a small pitchfork. The prongs plunge into the open mouth of a squat cylindrical glass jar of smooth caramel-brown spread sitting upright below; the spread has overflowed, pouring in heavy glossy ribbons over the jar's screw rim and down its sides, with a few thick rivulets running to the base and pooling on the ground.
scene.composition: Shoe occupies the upper-left and is cropped hard by the left canvas edge — roughly a third of the shoe (the back of the sole and part of the vamp) runs off-frame. Toe points up-right and nearly touches the 35% vertical. The heel/stem falls through the vertical centre of the left column at x≈24% and lands on the jar, which is centred on the same axis and scaled to about a fifth of the canvas width. Shoe and jar together form a single top-left to bottom-centre-left diagonal; nothing crosses into the right half.
scene.camera: Straight-on eye-level product view, long-lens feel with no perspective distortion, deep focus — everything is sharp front to back, no depth-of-field falloff.
scene.lighting: Bright, even studio lighting from the front-upper-left with a large soft source; strong specular highlights run along the shoe's top curve and the wet caramel ribbons. Shadows are almost entirely suppressed — only a faint soft contact shadow under the jar — so the objects read as cut-outs floating on white.
negative_space: Right half below the title: x=36%→100%, y=57%→92% — fully empty white
Upper right: x=40%→100%, y=0%→31% — empty white the title sits beneath
Band x=0%→100%, y=84%→92% — empty white the footer line sits on

font.family_guess: Bodoni Std / Didot (small-caps setting — initial B at full cap height, remaining letters at ~82% cap height)

elements.text: Don't be silly Andrea, everybody wants this.

ornaments.description: The 'I' of DEVIL is replaced by a devil-tail arrow: a single stroke that leaves the baseline, rises as a slightly curved diagonal up and to the right past the cap line, and ends in a solid two-barb arrowhead pointing up-right. Solid black, same weight as the letter stems, breaking the cap line of the word by about 5% of canvas height.

Three-pronged pitchfork/trident formed where the stiletto heel stem meets the jar — part of the rendered scene, but it reads as a graphic device: the caramel stem splits into three short tapered downward spikes entering the jar mouth.

why_it_works: The whole poster is one borrowed frame — a film title-card layout (tracked small line, huge serif name, small red verb, huge serif name) — so the joke lands before a single word is read.
Left half carries the image, right half carries the type, with a clean 11% gutter and nothing crossing it; the eye never has to separate figure from ground.

The red stiletto, the red of 'THE'/'EATS', the red jar label and the red footer line lock the entire page to a single hue against pure white, so the lone black title reads as the hardest contrast in frame.
